findings.problem: Both decrement theorems repeat the same step. They rebuild the positivity proofs for R/2^(i+1) and for (R/2^i)^2/4. They build `hnext` from `cutoffHeatGram_time_congr` and `dyadic_radius_square_succ`. Then they run `simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right, dyadicHeatGram_coe]` and `rw [hnext]` to rewrite the index-(i+1) Gram as the Gram at time (R/2^i)^2/4. The upper proof (lines 101-105) is the same block verbatim. The same block appears three more times in sibling files: DyadicHeatAt.lean (lines 68-73 and 118-122) and SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean (lines 77-81). A change to how `dyadicHeatGram` is indexed, or to `cutoffHeatGram`'s positivity arguments, would have to be made in all five places.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to `dyadicHeatGram_coe`. Its statement would be: `dyadicHeatGram_sub_inner (hR) (hlambda) (i) (v) : ⟪v, (dyadicHeatGram … i - dyadicHeatGram … (i+1)) v⟫_ℝ = ⟪v, (cutoffHeatGram … (sq_pos_of_pos hs) p lambda) v⟫_ℝ - ⟪v, (cutoffHeatGram … (ht : 0 < (R/2^i)^2/4) p lambda) v⟫_ℝ`, with `hs : 0 < R/2^i`. Its proof would be `simp only [sub_apply, inner_sub_right, dyadicHeatGram_coe]; rw [cutoffHeatGram_time_congr … (dyadic_radius_square_succ R i)]`. A coe-level companion `dyadicHeatGram_succ_coe` could be stated for the (i+1) Gram alone. In `dyadicHeatGram_lower`, the lines from `have hnext` to `rw [hnext]` are replaced by `rw [dyadicHeatGram_sub_inner μ hQ hk U χ hR hlambda i v]` after the existing `simp only [dyadicBochnerMass_inner, M.measure_real …]`, followed by `convert hb using 1; ring`. In `dyadicHeatGram_upper`, the same block is replaced by `rw [dyadicHeatGram_sub_inner …]`, followed by `simpa only [← hn] using hb`. The `*_at` variants in DyadicHeatAt.lean and SupportedHeatEnvelope.lean could use the same lemma, or a copy of it for `dyadicHeatGramAt`.
findings.benefit: The two theorems become shorter and show only their own estimates. The relation between consecutive dyadic Grams (time s^2 against s^2/4) is stated and proved once. It can also be reused by the three other proofs in the sibling files. A change to the Gram definition or the time-congruence lemma then needs one edit instead of five.
